**Daily Devotional**

**March 16**

*4 But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God. (Matthew 4:4 KJV)*

This was when Jesus was led by the spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil. Jesus quoted this from scripture (Deuteronomy 8:3), and used scripture to answer Satan every time he was tempted. This shows us that the best defense against the devil is to know scripture and quote it to him when we rebuke, and resist, him (James 4:7), and he will flee from us.

The Word of God is just as important to our wellbeing as food is. We must have food to live, and we must know the Word to live in all the blessings that God has given us, which is the only life worth living. Those who don’t feed on the Word of God are not spiritually healthy, as our bodies are not healthy without proper food. It is so awesome that we have a living God to worship, and one who was tempted in all ways as we are (Hebrews 4:15), to be our High Priest (Jesus). Praise God every day for all He has done, is doing, and will do for us his children. We have already been given all blessings, in spiritual form (Ephesians 1:3), and God does not, and can not, lie (Titus 1:2). Thank you Lord, for all your promises, and for your integrity.

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com

Look up the definition of the word retail.

By the dictionary definition you could argue that gasoline is a retail product, you could make the same argument for electricity, water, or natural gas.

My argument is that gasoline is better considered a commodity regardless of amount sold. Looking at how it reacts in markets is a better way to classify items as opposed to a language dictionary.
I think that you should look up the meanings of elastic demand and in inelastic demand as well.
There are plenty of commodities that have varying degrees of elasticity, and with petroleum fuels used half for industrial purposes gasoline is far from the most elastic.
